title: Start the book API
summary: Run the Reading List API on localhost and check its health address. Follow how Program.cs registers services and maps the book controller.
introduction: We have a project, a table and a connection setting. Now we can start the API. First we check that the web program is alive. Then the next lesson will check whether it can read Oracle rows.
learningObjectives: Start and stop the API using its launch profile
Read a health response without mistaking it for a database test
Find the services and controller route mapping

blocks.title: Run from the extracted sample root

blocks.text: Keep this terminal open. The launch profile uses http://localhost:5080 and the Development environment. Open a second terminal for requests. Press Ctrl+C in the first terminal when you want to stop the API.

blocks.content:
status         database
------         --------
API is running Not checked
blocks.title: Expected result

blocks.text: This reply says the API is running. It deliberately says that the database was not checked. A good health reply tells you exactly what was tested. Reading /api/books will test the real Oracle connection.

blocks.title: ReadingListApi/Program.cs

items: CreateBuilder reads settings and prepares the web app.
AddControllers enables classes that handle web requests.
AddScoped gives each request its own BookRepository helper.
AddOptions reads and checks the Oracle connection setting.
UseExceptionHandler sends a general error reply if a request fails.
MapGet adds the health address. MapControllers adds the book addresses. Run starts listening.

blocks.text: A **controller** groups related web actions. BooksController handles addresses that start with /api/books. The app asks the repository to do database work so the controller can stay focused on requests and replies.

blocks.title: Use local HTTP only for local practice
blocks.text: This sample listens on your own computer. A real public API needs HTTPS and an access plan before it handles other people's data. Publishing the lesson on GitHub Pages does not publish this API.
Read the two properties in the health reply. Stop the API with Ctrl+C and repeat the request. Start it again and check that the health request works once more.
